evidence.source: cargo test in hydragrow-shared (66 passed, 0 failed)
evidence.notes: Round-trip, Keep/Set/Clear semantics, provision validation, resolve, canonical topic, and Debug-redaction tests all pass.

evidence.environment: Host Rust tests + ESP-IDF source inspection (no ESP toolchain in this environment)
evidence.notes: prepare/commit/rollback and boot-decision unit tests pass. NVS write ordering (pending -> version -> Prepared) and boot commit-on-connect / rollback-and-reboot paths verified by inspection; ESP32 target build deferred to firmware-controller-ci.

evidence.environment: Host Rust tests + ESP-IDF source inspection
evidence.notes: OTA-only, keep/set/clear, and stale-version cases covered by host tests. Event ordering PrepareWifiConfig -> TriggerOtaUpdate, dispatcher freshness re-check, Keep resolution against NVS, metadata-only logging, and factory-reset pending cleanup verified by inspection.

evidence.source: cargo test in hydragrow-controller-core ota_verify (9 passed) + hw/ota.rs + .github/workflows/firmware-controller-release.yml (inspection)
evidence.notes: Same-version, downgrade, malformed, missing-sha256, and matching-sha256 cases pass. Device streams with SHA-256 and completes only on match; release uploads firmware.bin plus firmware.bin.sha256 with firmware.bin name unchanged.

evidence.source: cargo test in hydragrow-backend (226 passed, 0 failed, --test-threads=4) with migrations 20260907000000 applied on local Postgres
evidence.notes: DB schema contains no password column (asserted via to_jsonb row inspection). Metadata replace is per-device transactional; delivery pending/applied/stale-version behavior covered. OTA-only needs no wifi payload.
Matching applied/rolled_back recorded; stale, future, cross-device, and unknown states ignored; hostile password-smuggling payload deserializes without capture.

evidence.source: npm test -- --run in hydragrow-frontend (59 files, 262 tests) + npm run build
evidence.notes: OTA-only/combined enablement, blank masked keep-passwords, and pending/applied/rollback status rendering covered; production build succeeds.

evidence.source: device_identity host tests (5 passed) + local run of the release secret-dependency grep check (SECRET_CHECK_PASS)
evidence.notes: WIFI_SSID/PASSWORD/DEVICE_ID are option_env; NVS->default->MAC factory resolution with persistence; workflow no longer requires per-device secrets. ESP32 target build deferred to firmware-controller-ci.

evidence.source: cargo test device_ownership in hydragrow-backend (11 passed) incl. duplicate-hardware rejection
evidence.notes: Duplicate hardware binding returns ClaimError::DuplicateHardware mapped to HTTP 409; reclaim by same hardware and first-claim bootstrap pass. ProvisionDeviceId dispatcher arm verified by inspection.

evidence.source: redaction + throttle unit tests in hydragrow-shared/hydragrow-backend + main.rs MQTT transport code (inspection)
evidence.notes: Debug output contains no passwords; audit summary is metadata-only; 5 provisions per 300s per device; X-User-Confirmed retained; MQTT_TLS=1 selects native-TLS transport with no new plaintext path.

secret_store_statement: WiFi passwords exist durably only in the target ESP32 NVS (active wifi_list / pending keys). The Postgres schema (device_wifi_config, device_wifi_delivery, device_ownership) contains no password column; this is asserted by an integration test that inspects the stored row JSON.
